review.source: Actual written N1904 and the publisher rows, reviewed against the displayed BSB by Claude (Anthropic); independent peer review recorded in the registry.

7:1.sourceText: Καὶ μετὰ ταῦτα περιεπάτει ὁ Ἰησοῦς ἐν τῇ Γαλιλαίᾳ· οὐ γὰρ ἤθελεν ἐν τῇ Ἰουδαίᾳ περιπατεῖν, ὅτι ἐζήτουν αὐτὸν οἱ Ἰουδαῖοι ἀποκτεῖναι.
7:1.targetText: After this, Jesus traveled throughout Galilee. He did not want to travel in Judea, because the Jews there were trying to kill Him.

unmappedSource.reason: The opening καί only links to the previous section; BSB begins with After.
BSB starts a new sentence and leaves γάρ ("for") unrendered.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English adds there to point back to Judea.

7:2.sourceText: ἦν δὲ ἐγγὺς ἡ ἑορτὴ τῶν Ἰουδαίων ἡ σκηνοπηγία.
7:2.targetText: However, the Jewish Feast of Tabernacles was near.

groups.note: τῶν Ἰουδαίων ("of the Jews") is rendered Jewish.
The festival name σκηνοπηγία, in apposition to ἑορτή, is rendered (Feast) of Tabernacles.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

7:3.sourceText: εἶπον οὖν πρὸς αὐτὸν οἱ ἀδελφοὶ αὐτοῦ Μετάβηθι ἐντεῦθεν καὶ ὕπαγε εἰς τὴν Ἰουδαίαν, ἵνα καὶ οἱ μαθηταί σου θεωρήσουσιν τὰ ἔργα σοῦ ἃ ποιεῖς·
7:3.targetText: So Jesus’ brothers said to Him, “Leave here and go to Judea, so that Your disciples there may see the works You are doing.

groups.note: BSB names Jesus for the pronoun αὐτοῦ ("his").

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves καί ("also") unrendered.
BSB leaves the second σοῦ ("your") implicit in "the works You are doing".
The relative pronoun ἅ ("that") is left implicit in English.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English adds there (in Judea) to the disciples.

7:4.sourceText: οὐδεὶς γάρ τι ἐν κρυπτῷ ποιεῖ καὶ ζητεῖ αὐτὸς ἐν παρρησίᾳ εἶναι. εἰ ταῦτα ποιεῖς, φανέρωσον σεαυτὸν τῷ κόσμῳ.
7:4.targetText: For no one who wants to be known publicly acts in secret. Since You are doing these things, show Yourself to the world.”

groups.note: αὐτός, the person who seeks, is rendered by the relative who in BSB's recast.
ἐν παρρησίᾳ ("in openness") is rendered publicly.
εἶναι ἐν παρρησίᾳ ("to be in the open") is rendered to be known publicly.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves τι ("anything") implicit after acts.
BSB turns "and seeks" into the relative clause "who wants"; καί is not rendered.

7:5.sourceText: οὐδὲ γὰρ οἱ ἀδελφοὶ αὐτοῦ ἐπίστευον εἰς αὐτόν.
7:5.targetText: For even His own brothers did not believe in Him.

groups.note: οὐδέ ("not even") is split as even … not.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

7:6.sourceText: λέγει οὖν αὐτοῖς ὁ Ἰησοῦς Ὁ καιρὸς ὁ ἐμὸς οὔπω πάρεστιν, ὁ δὲ καιρὸς ὁ ὑμέτερος πάντοτέ ἐστιν ἕτοιμος.
7:6.targetText: Therefore Jesus told them, “Although your time is always at hand, My time has not yet come.

groups.note: BSB turns the contrast with δέ ("but") into a concessive Although clause.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

7:7.sourceText: οὐ δύναται ὁ κόσμος μισεῖν ὑμᾶς, ἐμὲ δὲ μισεῖ, ὅτι ἐγὼ μαρτυρῶ περὶ αὐτοῦ ὅτι τὰ ἔργα αὐτοῦ πονηρά ἐστιν.
7:7.targetText: The world cannot hate you, but it hates Me, because I testify that its works are evil.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves περὶ αὐτοῦ ("about it") implicit; the world is referred to by its in "its works".
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

7:8.sourceText: ὑμεῖς ἀνάβητε εἰς τὴν ἑορτήν· ἐγὼ οὔπω ἀναβαίνω εἰς τὴν ἑορτὴν ταύτην, ὅτι ὁ ἐμὸς καιρὸς οὔπω πεπλήρωται.
7:8.targetText: Go up to the feast on your own. I am not going up to this feast, because My time has not yet come.”

groups.note: The emphatic ὑμεῖς ("you yourselves") is rendered on your own.

unmappedSource.reason: N1904 reads οὔπω ("not yet"); BSB's Greek text differs at this word, and its "I am not going up" does not render οὔπω.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: BSB's "not" follows a different reading here; N1904 has οὔπω ("not yet").

7:9.sourceText: ταῦτα δὲ εἰπὼν αὐτοῖς ἔμεινεν ἐν τῇ Γαλιλαίᾳ.
7:9.targetText: Having said this, Jesus remained in Galilee.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves δέ unrendered.
BSB has no "to them" here; its Greek differs from N1904 at this word.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English names the subject of remained.

7:10.sourceText: Ὡς δὲ ἀνέβησαν οἱ ἀδελφοὶ αὐτοῦ εἰς τὴν ἑορτήν, τότε καὶ αὐτὸς ἀνέβη, οὐ φανερῶς ἀλλὰ ὡς ἐν κρυπτῷ.
7:10.targetText: But after His brothers had gone up to the feast, He also went—not publicly, but in secret.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
BSB leaves τότε ("then") unrendered after the after-clause.
BSB leaves ὡς ("as it were") unrendered.

7:11.sourceText: οἱ οὖν Ἰουδαῖοι ἐζήτουν αὐτὸν ἐν τῇ ἑορτῇ καὶ ἔλεγον Ποῦ ἐστιν ἐκεῖνος;
7:11.targetText: So the Jews were looking for Him at the feast and asking, “Where is He?”

7:12.sourceText: καὶ γογγυσμὸς περὶ αὐτοῦ ἦν πολὺς ἐν τοῖς ὄχλοις· οἱ μὲν ἔλεγον ὅτι Ἀγαθός ἐστιν, ἄλλοι δὲ ἔλεγον Οὔ, ἀλλὰ πλανᾷ τὸν ὄχλον.
7:12.targetText: Many in the crowds were whispering about Him. Some said, “He is a good man.”  But others replied, “No, He deceives the people.”

groups.note: "There was much murmuring" is recast as Many … were whispering.

unmappedSource.reason: The opening καί only links to the previous verse.
The μέν … δέ contrast is carried by But.
Recitative ὅτι introducing direct speech is not rendered.
BSB leaves ἀλλά ("rather") unrendered after No.

7:13.sourceText: οὐδεὶς μέντοι παρρησίᾳ ἐλάλει περὶ αὐτοῦ διὰ τὸν φόβον τῶν Ἰουδαίων.
7:13.targetText: Yet no one would speak publicly about Him for fear of the Jews.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

7:14.sourceText: Ἤδη δὲ τῆς ἑορτῆς μεσούσης ἀνέβη Ἰησοῦς εἰς τὸ ἱερὸν καὶ ἐδίδασκεν.
7:14.targetText: About halfway through the feast, Jesus went up to the temple courts and began to teach.

groups.note: The genitive absolute "the feast being at its midpoint" is rendered About halfway through the feast.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves ἤδη ("already") unrendered.
BSB leaves δέ unrendered.

7:15.sourceText: ἐθαύμαζον οὖν οἱ Ἰουδαῖοι λέγοντες Πῶς οὗτος γράμματα οἶδεν μὴ μεμαθηκώς;
7:15.targetText: The Jews were amazed and asked, “How did this man attain such learning without having studied?”

groups.note: οἶδεν ("knows") is rendered did … attain.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves οὖν unrendered.

unmappedTarget.reason: English joins the participle λέγοντες to the main verb.

7:16.sourceText: ἀπεκρίθη οὖν αὐτοῖς Ἰησοῦς καὶ εἶπεν Ἡ ἐμὴ διδαχὴ οὐκ ἔστιν ἐμὴ ἀλλὰ τοῦ πέμψαντός με·
7:16.targetText: “My teaching is not My own,” Jesus replied. “It comes from Him who sent Me.

groups.note: ἀπεκρίθη … καὶ εἶπεν ("answered and said") is rendered replied.
τοῦ πέμψαντος ("of the one who sent") is rendered from Him who sent.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves οὖν unrendered.
BSB leaves αὐτοῖς ("to them") implicit.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
BSB starts a new sentence instead of rendering ἀλλά ("but").

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies a subject and verb for the new sentence.

7:17.sourceText: ἐάν τις θέλῃ τὸ θέλημα αὐτοῦ ποιεῖν, γνώσεται περὶ τῆς διδαχῆς, πότερον ἐκ τοῦ Θεοῦ ἐστιν ἢ ἐγὼ ἀπ’ ἐμαυτοῦ λαλῶ.
7:17.targetText: If anyone desires to do His will, he will know whether My teaching is from God or whether I speak on My own.

groups.note: The article is rendered as the possessive My.
English repeats whether for the second alternative.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
BSB makes the teaching the subject of the whether-clause, so περί ("about") is not rendered.

7:18.sourceText: ὁ ἀφ’ ἑαυτοῦ λαλῶν τὴν δόξαν τὴν ἰδίαν ζητεῖ· ὁ δὲ ζητῶν τὴν δόξαν τοῦ πέμψαντος αὐτὸν, οὗτος ἀληθής ἐστιν καὶ ἀδικία ἐν αὐτῷ οὐκ ἔστιν.
7:18.targetText: He who speaks on his own authority seeks his own glory, but He who seeks the glory of the One who sent Him is a man of truth; in Him there is no falsehood.

groups.note: ἀφ’ ἑαυτοῦ ("from himself") is rendered on his own authority.
The adjective ἀληθής ("true") is rendered a man of truth.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
The resumptive οὗτος ("this one") is not rendered; BSB keeps "He who seeks" as the subject.
BSB uses a semicolon instead of καί.

7:19.sourceText: οὐ Μωϋσῆς ἔδωκεν ὑμῖν τὸν νόμον; καὶ οὐδεὶς ἐξ ὑμῶν ποιεῖ τὸν νόμον. τί με ζητεῖτε ἀποκτεῖναι;
7:19.targetText: Has not Moses given you the law? Yet not one of you keeps it. Why are you trying to kill Me?”

groups.note: Same verb, in another form in BSB's Greek text.
τὸν νόμον ("the law") is rendered it.

7:20.sourceText: ἀπεκρίθη ὁ ὄχλος Δαιμόνιον ἔχεις· τίς σε ζητεῖ ἀποκτεῖναι;
7:20.targetText: “You have a demon,” the crowd replied. “Who is trying to kill You?”

7:21.sourceText: ἀπεκρίθη Ἰησοῦς καὶ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς Ἓν ἔργον ἐποίησα καὶ πάντες θαυμάζετε.
7:21.targetText: Jesus answered them, “I did one miracle, and you are all amazed.

groups.note: ἀπεκρίθη … καὶ εἶπεν ("answered and said") is rendered answered.

7:22.sourceText: διὰ τοῦτο Μωϋσῆς δέδωκεν ὑμῖν τὴν περιτομήν, —οὐχ ὅτι ἐκ τοῦ Μωϋσέως ἐστὶν ἀλλ’ ἐκ τῶν πατέρων,— καὶ ἐν σαββάτῳ περιτέμνετε ἄνθρωπον.
7:22.targetText: But because Moses gave you circumcision, you circumcise a boy on the Sabbath (not that it is from Moses, but from the patriarchs.)

groups.note: διὰ τοῦτο ("because of this") is rendered because, introducing BSB's cause clause.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
BSB's because-clause replaces the link with καί ("and").

unmappedTarget.reason: English adds a contrast with the previous verse.
English supplies an article before Sabbath; the Greek has none.

7:23.sourceText: εἰ περιτομὴν λαμβάνει ἄνθρωπος ἐν σαββάτῳ ἵνα μὴ λυθῇ ὁ νόμος Μωϋσέως, ἐμοὶ χολᾶτε ὅτι ὅλον ἄνθρωπον ὑγιῆ ἐποίησα ἐν σαββάτῳ;
7:23.targetText: If a boy can be circumcised on the Sabbath so that the law of Moses will not be broken, why are you angry with Me for making the whole man well on the Sabbath?

groups.note: περιτομὴν λαμβάνει ("receives circumcision") is rendered can be circumcised.

unmappedTarget.reason: BSB phrases the yes/no question "are you angry with Me?" as a why-question.
English supplies an article before Sabbath; the Greek has none.
English supplies an article before whole man; the Greek has none.
English supplies an article before Sabbath; the Greek has none.

7:24.sourceText: μὴ κρίνετε κατ’ ὄψιν, ἀλλὰ τὴν δικαίαν κρίσιν κρίνατε.
7:24.targetText: Stop judging by outward appearances, and start judging justly.”

groups.note: The present prohibition μὴ κρίνετε ("do not keep judging") is rendered Stop judging.
ἀλλά ("but rather") is rendered and.
τὴν δικαίαν κρίσιν ("the righteous judgment") is rendered justly.
Same verb, in another form in BSB's Greek text.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

7:25.sourceText: Ἔλεγον οὖν τινες ἐκ τῶν Ἱεροσολυμειτῶν Οὐχ οὗτός ἐστιν ὃν ζητοῦσιν ἀποκτεῖναι;
7:25.targetText: Then some of the people of Jerusalem began to say, “Isn’t this the man they are trying to kill?

groups.note: Same word, spelled differently in BSB's Greek text; "the Jerusalemites" is rendered the people of Jerusalem.
The relative ὅν ("whom") is rendered the man.

7:26.sourceText: καὶ ἴδε παρρησίᾳ λαλεῖ καὶ οὐδὲν αὐτῷ λέγουσιν. Μή ποτε ἀληθῶς ἔγνωσαν οἱ ἄρχοντες ὅτι οὗτός ἐστιν ὁ Χριστός;
7:26.targetText: Yet here He is, speaking publicly, and they are not saying anything to Him. Have the rulers truly recognized that this is the Christ?

unmappedSource.reason: BSB renders the hesitant question Μή ποτε ("can it be that …?") as a plain question.

7:27.sourceText: ἀλλὰ τοῦτον οἴδαμεν πόθεν ἐστίν· ὁ δὲ Χριστὸς ὅταν ἔρχηται, οὐδεὶς γινώσκει πόθεν ἐστίν.
7:27.targetText: But we know where this man is from. When the Christ comes, no one will know where He is from.”

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves δέ unrendered.

7:28.sourceText: ἔκραξεν οὖν ἐν τῷ ἱερῷ διδάσκων ὁ Ἰησοῦς καὶ λέγων Κἀμὲ οἴδατε καὶ οἴδατε πόθεν εἰμί· καὶ ἀπ’ ἐμαυτοῦ οὐκ ἐλήλυθα, ἀλλ’ ἔστιν ἀληθινὸς ὁ πέμψας με, ὃν ὑμεῖς οὐκ οἴδατε·
7:28.targetText: Then Jesus, still teaching in the temple courts, cried out, “You know Me, and you know where I am from. I have not come of My own accord, but He who sent Me is true. You do not know Him,

groups.note: ἀπ’ ἐμαυτοῦ ("from Myself") is rendered of My own accord.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
καὶ λέγων ("and saying") is represented only by the quotation.
BSB starts a new sentence and leaves καί unrendered.

unmappedTarget.reason: English adds still; the Greek has only the participle teaching.

7:29.sourceText: ἐγὼ οἶδα αὐτόν, ὅτι παρ’ αὐτοῦ εἰμι κἀκεῖνός με ἀπέστειλεν.
7:29.targetText: but I know Him, because I am from Him and He sent Me.”

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies the contrast with "You do not know Him"; the Greek has no connective here.

7:30.sourceText: Ἐζήτουν οὖν αὐτὸν πιάσαι, καὶ οὐδεὶς ἐπέβαλεν ἐπ’ αὐτὸν τὴν χεῖρα, ὅτι οὔπω ἐληλύθει ἡ ὥρα αὐτοῦ.
7:30.targetText: So they tried to seize Him, but no one laid a hand on Him, because His hour had not yet come.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

7:31.sourceText: Ἐκ τοῦ ὄχλου δὲ πολλοὶ ἐπίστευσαν εἰς αὐτόν, καὶ ἔλεγον Ὁ Χριστὸς ὅταν ἔλθῃ, μὴ πλείονα σημεῖα ποιήσει ὧν οὗτος ἐποίησεν;
7:31.targetText: Many in the crowd, however, believed in Him and said, “When the Christ comes, will He perform more signs than this man?”

unmappedSource.reason: BSB renders the question particle μή (expecting "no") as a plain question.
BSB leaves ἐποίησεν ("has done") implicit after than this man.

7:32.sourceText: Ἤκουσαν οἱ Φαρισαῖοι τοῦ ὄχλου γογγύζοντος περὶ αὐτοῦ ταῦτα, καὶ ἀπέστειλαν οἱ ἀρχιερεῖς καὶ οἱ Φαρισαῖοι ὑπηρέτας ἵνα πιάσωσιν αὐτόν.
7:32.targetText: When the Pharisees heard the crowd whispering these things about Jesus, they and the chief priests sent officers to arrest Him.

groups.note: BSB names Jesus for the pronoun αὐτοῦ ("him").
BSB turns "heard … and sent" into "When … heard …, they … sent".
οἱ Φαρισαῖοι ("the Pharisees"), just named, is rendered they.

7:33.sourceText: εἶπεν οὖν ὁ Ἰησοῦς Ἔτι χρόνον μικρὸν μεθ’ ὑμῶν εἰμι καὶ ὑπάγω πρὸς τὸν πέμψαντά με.
7:33.targetText: So Jesus said, “I am with you only a little while longer, and then I am going to the One who sent Me.

groups.note: Ἔτι ("still") is rendered longer.
χρόνον μικρόν ("a little time") is rendered a little while.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English adds only for emphasis.

7:34.sourceText: ζητήσετέ με καὶ οὐχ εὑρήσετέ, καὶ ὅπου εἰμὶ ἐγὼ ὑμεῖς οὐ δύνασθε ἐλθεῖν.
7:34.targetText: You will look for Me, but you will not find Me; and where I am, you cannot come.”

unmappedTarget.reason: BSB follows a reading with an extra word here.

7:35.sourceText: εἶπον οὖν οἱ Ἰουδαῖοι πρὸς ἑαυτούς Ποῦ οὗτος μέλλει πορεύεσθαι, ὅτι ἡμεῖς οὐχ εὑρήσομεν αὐτόν; μὴ εἰς τὴν Διασπορὰν τῶν Ἑλλήνων μέλλει πορεύεσθαι καὶ διδάσκειν τοὺς Ἕλληνας;
7:35.targetText: At this, the Jews said to one another, “Where does He intend to go that we will not find Him? Will He go where the Jews are dispersed among the Greeks, and teach the Greeks?

groups.note: τὴν Διασποράν ("the Dispersion") is rendered where the Jews are dispersed.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB renders the question particle μή (expecting "no") as a plain question.

7:36.sourceText: τίς ἐστιν ὁ λόγος οὗτος ὃν εἶπεν Ζητήσετέ με καὶ οὐχ εὑρήσετέ, καὶ ὅπου εἰμὶ ἐγὼ ὑμεῖς οὐ δύνασθε ἐλθεῖν;
7:36.targetText: What does He mean by saying, ‘You will look for Me, but you will not find Me,’ and, ‘Where I am, you cannot come’?”

groups.note: τίς ἐστιν ὁ λόγος οὗτος ("what is this statement") is recast as What does He mean.
ὃν εἶπεν ("which He said") is rendered by saying.

unmappedTarget.reason: BSB follows a reading with an extra word here.

7:37.sourceText: Ἐν δὲ τῇ ἐσχάτῃ ἡμέρᾳ τῇ μεγάλῃ τῆς ἑορτῆς εἱστήκει ὁ Ἰησοῦς, καὶ ἔκραξεν λέγων Ἐάν τις διψᾷ, ἐρχέσθω πρός με καὶ πινέτω.
7:37.targetText: On the last and greatest day of the feast, Jesus stood up and called out in a loud voice, “If anyone is thirsty, let him come to Me and drink.

targetPhrases.text: called out in a loud voice

groups.note: ἔκραξεν ("cried out") is rendered called out in a loud voice.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves δέ unrendered.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
λέγων ("saying") is represented only by the quotation.

unmappedTarget.reason: English joins the two adjectives last and greatest.

7:38.sourceText: ὁ πιστεύων εἰς ἐμέ, καθὼς εἶπεν ἡ γραφή, ποταμοὶ ἐκ τῆς κοιλίας αὐτοῦ ῥεύσουσιν ὕδατος ζῶντος.
7:38.targetText: Whoever believes in Me, as the Scripture has said: ‘Streams of living water will flow from within him.’”

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

7:39.sourceText: τοῦτο δὲ εἶπεν περὶ τοῦ Πνεύματος οὗ ἔμελλον λαμβάνειν οἱ πιστεύσαντες εἰς αὐτόν· οὔπω γὰρ ἦν Πνεῦμα, ὅτι Ἰησοῦς οὐδέπω ἐδοξάσθη.
7:39.targetText: He was speaking about the Spirit, whom those who believed in Him were later to receive. For the Spirit had not yet been given, because Jesus had not yet been glorified.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves τοῦτο ("this") implicit in He was speaking about.
BSB leaves δέ unrendered.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies an article before Spirit; the Greek has none.
English supplies given; the Greek says only that the Spirit "was not yet".

7:40.sourceText: Ἐκ τοῦ ὄχλου οὖν ἀκούσαντες τῶν λόγων τούτων ἔλεγον Οὗτός ἐστιν ἀληθῶς ὁ προφήτης·
7:40.targetText: On hearing these words, some of the people said, “This is truly the Prophet.”

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves οὖν unrendered.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

7:41.sourceText: ἄλλοι ἔλεγον Οὗτός ἐστιν ὁ Χριστός· οἱ δὲ ἔλεγον Μὴ γὰρ ἐκ τῆς Γαλιλαίας ὁ Χριστὸς ἔρχεται;
7:41.targetText: Others declared, “This is the Christ.”  But still others asked, “How can the Christ come from Galilee?

groups.note: The article οἱ used as a pronoun ("others") is rendered still others.
Μὴ γάρ introduces an incredulous question expecting "no", rendered How can …?

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

7:42.sourceText: οὐχ ἡ γραφὴ εἶπεν ὅτι ἐκ τοῦ σπέρματος Δαυεὶδ, καὶ ἀπὸ Βηθλεὲμ τῆς κώμης ὅπου ἦν Δαυεὶδ, ἔρχεται ὁ Χριστός;
7:42.targetText: Doesn’t the Scripture say that the Christ will come from the line of David and from Bethlehem, the village where David lived?”

7:43.sourceText: σχίσμα οὖν ἐγένετο ἐν τῷ ὄχλῳ δι’ αὐτόν·
7:43.targetText: So there was division in the crowd because of Jesus.

groups.note: BSB names Jesus for the pronoun αὐτόν ("him").

7:44.sourceText: τινὲς δὲ ἤθελον ἐξ αὐτῶν πιάσαι αὐτόν, ἀλλ’ οὐδεὶς ἐπέβαλεν ἐπ’ αὐτὸν τὰς χεῖρας.
7:44.targetText: Some of them wanted to seize Him, but no one laid a hand on Him.

groups.note: The plural χεῖρας ("hands") is rendered a hand.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves δέ unrendered.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

7:45.sourceText: Ἦλθον οὖν οἱ ὑπηρέται πρὸς τοὺς ἀρχιερεῖς καὶ Φαρισαίους, καὶ εἶπον αὐτοῖς ἐκεῖνοι Διὰ τί οὐκ ἠγάγετε αὐτόν;
7:45.targetText: Then the officers returned to the chief priests and Pharisees, who asked them, “Why didn’t you bring Him in?”

groups.note: The demonstrative ἐκεῖνοι ("those") is rendered by the relative who.
Διὰ τί ("for what reason") is rendered Why.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB turns "and those said" into a relative who-clause; καί is not rendered.

7:46.sourceText: ἀπεκρίθησαν οἱ ὑπηρέται Οὐδέποτε ἐλάλησεν οὕτως ἄνθρωπος, ὡς οὗτος λαλεῖ ὁ ἄνθρωπος.
